run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The orders-fulfillment consumption path in namespace astronomy-shop is stalled: the pod orders-validator-6d49bfb98d-xnww2 (Deployment orders-validator, consuming Kafka topic orders-fulfillment) successfully processed the pre-existing orders ORD-100000..ORD-100019 (committing offsets 1..20), then at 2026-11-21T13:29:58.387Z hit a record at offset 20 that is not valid JSON — 'record validation failed at offset=20: Expecting value: line 1 column 35 (char 34)' — and logged 'partition processing paused at offset=20'. It never commits past offset 20: the consumer group orders-validator showed committed_offset 20 against end_offset 83 (lag 63) at 13:31:54 and total_lag 145 at 13:34:38, while the producer order-stream kept publishing valid 'published order_id=ORD-...' records every ~2s. The Kafka topic itself (1 partition, leader 1, in-sync, not under-replicated) and the rest of the Astronomy Shop were checked and look healthy in the sampled 13:28:40–13:30:13 window: all 25 deployments 1/1 ready, all 29 pods Running with 0 restarts, every Service endpoint has ready addresses, checkout PlaceOrder spans completed with gRPC status 0 in 32–47 ms, the app's own Kafka consumers accounting (lag 0) and fraud-detection (lag 1) on topic orders are keeping up, locust's failure ratio fell to 0 by 13:30:00 after startup-only errors, and every flagd fault flag is defaultVariant 'off' with no flag reload during the window. The evidence pins the blockage on the malformed record at offset 20 of orders-fulfillment and on the consumer's fail-stop handling; which writer emitted that record before order-stream started publishing (Kafka topic data was pre-seeded with ORD-100000..ORD-100019 plus this bad record) could not be established from the available tools, so the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: orders-validator-6d49bfb98d-xnww2 (Deployment orders-validator) logged: 'orders-validator started bootstrap=kafka:9092 topic=orders-fulfillment group=orders-validator', 'resuming partition at offset=0', then 'processed order_id=ORD-100000 .. ORD-100019 committed_offset=1..20', and at 13:29:58.387Z 'ERROR record validation failed at offset=20: Expecting value: line 1 column 35 (char 34)' immediately followed by 'ERROR partition processing paused at offset=20'.

Consumer group orders-validator was STABLE with one member assigned to orders-fulfillment partition 0, committed_offset 20, log_start_offset 0, end_offset 83 and lag 63 (observed 13:31:54); a later query of the same topic reported total_lag 145 for that group (observed 13:34:38), so the backlog is growing rather than draining.

The producer order-stream-5c7cc84b47-fl4dp kept publishing successfully during the window: 'published order_id=ORD-27FF3007B14C' at 13:29:52.182Z through 'published order_id=ORD-0F3D8FBA136A' at 13:30:12.216Z at a ~2s interval, i.e. the producer is running and its records are not the blocked consumption step.

Kafka cluster has topics __consumer_offsets, orders, orders-fulfillment and orders-processed; orders-fulfillment has one partition (leader 1, replicas [1], isr [1], offline false, under_replicated false), and order-stream and orders-validator are configured with ORDERS_TOPIC=orders-fulfillment and OUTPUT_TOPIC=orders-processed / CONSUMER_GROUP=orders-validator.

The consumer code mounted into orders-validator from ConfigMap orders-pipeline-scripts (/scripts/consumer.py, mounted via volume 'scripts') has no poison-message handling: on any exception in process() it logs 'record validation failed' and 'partition processing paused', then sleeps in an infinite loop and never commits or skips, which is why one bad record halts the whole single-partition topic.

The malformed record at orders-fulfillment offset 20 was written by the environment's data seeding step rather than by the running order-stream: the records just before the failure are a synthetic sequential series ORD-100000..ORD-100019, the failing record is the next one (offset 20), and the offset arithmetic is consistent with roughly 21 pre-existing records (end_offset 83 at 13:31:54 versus ~62 records published by order-stream since its first publish at 13:29:52). Message content is not readable with the available tools, so the actual writer of offset 20 remains unproven.

The rest of the Astronomy Shop workload was checked and is up: all 25 deployments in astronomy-shop report 1 ready / 1 available / 1 replica / 1 updated, and all 29 pods are Running with restart count 0 (started 13:28:40–13:29:57).

All 23 Service endpoints in astronomy-shop have ready backend addresses and none have not-ready addresses (for example ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, payment, product-catalog, product-reviews, recommendation, shipping each 1 ready; otel-collector 3 ready), so no service lacks endpoints.

Checkout's own order flow is working in the sampled window: checkout spans oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder carry rpc.grpc.status_code 0 with durations 47 ms, 34 ms and 32 ms, oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge returns rpc.grpc.status_code 0, 'publish orders' spans complete in 0.3–0.4 ms, and the load-generator POST plus frontend-proxy spans carry http.status_code 200.

The application's own Kafka consumers on topic orders are keeping up: group accounting has committed_offset 22 = end_offset 22 (lag 0) and group fraud-detection has committed_offset 21 against end_offset 22 (lag 1), and accounting logs show it receiving and processing order details (e.g. orderId 90be4560-e5af-11f1-9baa-a621163236be at 13:29:24, a723c648-... at 13:30:01).

The load generator's end-user error signal is not continuous: locust_requests_fail_ratio was 0.25 at 13:29:00 and 0.0787 at 13:29:30 (while pods were still starting) and 0 at 13:30:00, and the cumulative locust_errors are the startup 5xx (3x POST /api/checkout, 1x GET/POST /api/cart, 1x /api/recommendations, 1x /api/product-reviews) reported at 13:29:33; no end-user failure is observed after the shop finished starting.

Fault injection through flagd feature flags is rejected for this window: ConfigMap flagd-config (demo.flagd.json) has all 15 flags (adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, imageSlowLoad, llmRateLimitError, llmInaccurateResponse, emailMemoryLeak, failedReadinessProbe, adHighCpu, adManualGc, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage) ENABLED with defaultVariant 'off', and the flagd container loaded the file at 13:28:45 with no later reload logged inside the window.

The firing HighRequestLatency alert on service_name=accounting (value 5e+03 ms, activeAt 13:31:26) is not supported as a real latency fault inside the authorized window: accounting's own span duration buckets at 13:30:00 show all 2 'otel' client spans at or below 250 ms (le=250 count 2) and its single 'receive orders' consumer span at or below 75 ms, so the 5000 ms p95 is a small-sample histogram artifact rather than measured latency.

The namespace was brought up from zero at 13:28:40–13:29:57 (events 'Scaled up replica set <name> from 0 to 1' for all deployments, pod Started/Scheduled events), and the only Unhealthy events in astronomy-shop are startup readiness/startup-probe misses on otel-collector-agent-cgf6d, otel-collector-agent-jv9g7, grafana-7b9cbf56f5-sqzrg and opensearch-0 between 13:28:46 and 13:29:10 (plus one FailedMount on otel-collector-agent-jv9g7 at 13:28:41).

If the malformed record at orders-fulfillment offset 20 is removed or skipped and the consumer is made to log-and-commit past invalid records, the lag of at least 63 (later 145) unprocessed records should drain, because the producer order-stream and the broker are both healthy and only the poisoned offset blocks the single partition.

Inspect the record at orders-fulfillment partition 0 offset 20 with a Kafka client outside this investigation, then either replace/delete it or commit the group past it; additionally change orders-validator so a single unparseable record cannot pause the partition (log, count and skip), and confirm total_lag returns to 0 afterwards.

gaps: Message content of Kafka topic orders-fulfillment is not readable with the available Kafka tools, so the exact bytes of the failing record at offset 20 and the identity of the writer that produced it could not be verified.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so when and by which actor (seed script, fault injector or producer) offset 20 of orders-fulfillment was written cannot be established.
Only the consumer's view of the poison record exists ('Expecting value: line 1 column 35 (char 34)'); whether the record is truncated or has a corrupted byte is inferred and unverified.

Prometheus span metrics for astronomy-shop only have samples from about 13:29–13:30 (stack started 13:28:40), so there is no baseline before 13:28:40 and any pre-existing application behaviour in the 24h window is unknown; traces are limited to what Jaeger kept since its 13:28:48 restart.
Content/offsets of topic orders-processed were not observable, so whether any record was ever successfully forwarded downstream by orders-validator is unknown.

The HighRequestLatency alert for accounting was observed only at 13:32:26 (after the authorized window end 13:30:13), so its state during the window is unknown and it cannot be confirmed or excluded as a during-window symptom.
next_steps: Use a Kafka client with content access to dump orders-fulfillment partition 0 offset 20 and confirm the malformed payload and its producer headers.
Check the task environment's data-seeding or fault-injection job (change history is not integrated here) to confirm whether it deliberately wrote the corrupt record at offset 20.
After clearing or skipping the poison record, re-check the orders-validator consumer group lag to confirm it drains to 0 and that records appear on orders-processed.
Keep monitoring orders-validator and order-stream, since the consumer's fail-stop script will halt the single-partition pipeline again on any future unparseable record.

import json
import logging
import os
import signal
import time

from confluent_kafka import Consumer, Producer

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
log = logging.getLogger("orders-validator")

BOOTSTRAP = os.environ.get("KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP", "kafka:9092")
TOPIC = os.environ.get("ORDERS_TOPIC", "orders-fulfillment")
OUTPUT_TOPIC = os.environ.get("OUTPUT_TOPIC", "orders-processed")
GROUP = os.environ.get("CONSUMER_GROUP", "orders-validator")

_shutdown = False


def _request_shutdown(signum, frame):
    global _shutdown
    _shutdown = True


def process(value):
    obj = json.loads(value.decode("utf-8"))
    if "order_id" not in obj:
        raise ValueError("record has no 'order_id' field")
    return obj


def main():
    consumer = Consumer(
        {
            "bootstrap.servers": BOOTSTRAP,
            "group.id": GROUP,
            "enable.auto.commit": False,
            "auto.offset.reset": "earliest",
            "max.poll.interval.ms": 86400000,
        }
    )
    out = Producer({"bootstrap.servers": BOOTSTRAP, "enable.idempotence": True})
    consumer.subscribe([TOPIC])
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _request_shutdown)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, _request_shutdown)
    log.info("orders-validator started bootstrap=%s topic=%s group=%s", BOOTSTRAP, TOPIC, GROUP)

    first = True
    while not _shutdown:
        msg = consumer.poll(1.0)
        if msg is None:
            continue
        if msg.error():
            log.warning("consumer error: %s", msg.error())
            continue

        if first:
            log.info("resuming partition at offset=%d", msg.offset())
            first = False

        try:
            order = process(msg.value())
        except Exception as exc:
            log.error("record validation failed at offset=%d: %s", msg.offset(), exc)
            log.error("partition processing paused at offset=%d", msg.offset())
            blocked = 0
            while not _shutdown:
                time.sleep(1)
                blocked += 1
                if blocked % 15 == 0:
                    log.error("partition remains paused at offset=%d", msg.offset())
            break

        result = json.dumps(
            {"source_offset": msg.offset(), "order_id": order["order_id"]},
            separators=(",", ":"),
        )
        out.produce(OUTPUT_TOPIC, value=result.encode("utf-8"))
        out.flush(10)
        consumer.commit(message=msg, asynchronous=False)
        log.info("processed order_id=%s committed_offset=%d", order["order_id"], msg.offset() + 1)

    out.flush(10)
    consumer.close()
    log.info("orders-validator stopped")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import json
import logging
import os
import time
import uuid

from confluent_kafka import Producer

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
log = logging.getLogger("order-stream")

BOOTSTRAP = os.environ.get("KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP", "kafka:9092")
TOPIC = os.environ.get("ORDERS_TOPIC", "orders-fulfillment")
INTERVAL = float(os.environ.get("PRODUCE_INTERVAL_SEC", "2.0"))


def main():
    producer = Producer({"bootstrap.servers": BOOTSTRAP, "enable.idempotence": True})
    while True:
        order_id = "ORD-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:12].upper()
        record = json.dumps({"order_id": order_id, "amount": 1 + int(uuid.uuid4().hex[:2], 16) % 7})
        producer.produce(TOPIC, value=record.encode("utf-8"))
        producer.poll(0)
        producer.flush(10)
        log.info("published order_id=%s", order_id)
        time.sleep(INTERVAL)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
